51226544.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to HDAC4 catalytic domain (648 to 1057 residues) (unknown origin) by surface plasmon resonance analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) using a CM5 sensor chip. The HDAC4 catalytic domain (residues 648–1057) was immobilized on the chip via amine coupling. The ligand, compound 16 or 22, was injected at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 nM in HBS-EP buffer (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20) at a flow rate of 30 μL/min. Association and dissociation phases were 180 s and 600 s, respectively. Regeneration was achieved with 10 mM glycine-HCl, pH 2.0. Data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The affinity (KD) and rate constants (kon, koff) were determined by global fitting of the sensorgrams to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. Co-crystal X-ray structure of pyrimidine hydroxamic acid 16 at 2.1 Å resolution (PDB code 6FYZ).
original_paragraph.Results section: The affinity (KD) and binding rate constants (kon and koff) of 16 and 22 to the catalytic domain of immobilized HDAC4 were also determined by surface plasmon resonance technology (Table S1). The KD values were in good agreement with biochemical IC50 for each compound.

assay_conditions.running_buffer_composition: HBS-EP buffer (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20)
